text:
incident-bot: Paging laura (oncall): p99 latency spike detected for streaming endpoints in eu-west2. Current alert: streaming-tail-latency > 1200ms for 10m. See metric dashboard: https://redwood.app/dash/streaming-eu-west2
laura (oncall): I'm up, taking. any customer-facing impact?
mike (sre): We're seeing elevated p95/p99 across streaming gateway -> nat path. p95 ~ 350ms (normal ~120), p99 ~ 1.3s. Tail stalls on chunked responses, some connections in CLOSE_WAIT.
raj (network): Traces show increased TLS handshake times originating in az-b -> az-c egress path. Lots of retransmits and SYN retries between NATs. Packetloss ~0.6% and intermittent DNS timeouts for some subnets.
emily (support): I've got one active customer report — v. early but they mention streaming stalls and partial transcripts. SLA impact?
laura (oncall): Mark customer as potentially impacted, set status page to maintenance? hold — need confirmation.
mike (sre): Quick runbook steps: 1) verify NAT ephemeral port exhaustion 2) check conntrack table sizes 3) fallback routing path to avoid hairpin. Running: `ss -s; iptables -L -n -v` on gateway boxes.
raj (network): Confirmed NAT ephemeral ports trending high in eu-west2-nat-1 (80% ephemeral usage). BGP path flips observed between az-b and az-c for a subset of flows. Also DNS queries to 10.2.0.10 show ~30% SERVFAIL spikes.
laura (oncall): Start mitigation: (A) enable ephemeral port reuse + lower TIME_WAIT on NATs, (B) increase conntrack limit on edge nodes, (C) failover a subset of streaming traffic to eu-west2-nat-2. Can someone run the config changes?
raj (network): I'll promote eu-west2-nat-2 into active pool for streaming route. Applying `aws ec2 modify-network-interface` equivalent to shift primary IPs, and update route weight policy.
mike (sre): I'm increasing conntrack max on all gateway hosts: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=500000` and adjusting `net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1` and `net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=15`. Pushing via orchestration now.
sam (eng-runtime): On the runtime side, enabling automatic smaller chunk sizes and increasing request-level reconnect backoff to reduce parallel handshakes. Patching streaming proxy config: `max_concurrent_handshakes: 50` temporarily.
emily (support): Noted. Posting a cautious note to the affected customers list that we're investigating streaming latency.
laura (oncall): Incident timeline to do: 1) apply network mitigations 2) watch p95/p99 and streaming stalls 3) if not improving in 10m, start graceful POD restarts for gateway pool 4) prepare rollback plan.
mike (sre): After conntrack bump and TIME_WAIT changes we're seeing ephemeral usage drop to 52% on nat-1 and 18% traffic now routed via nat-2. p95 dropped to ~180ms within 3m. p99 trending down to ~680ms. Some tail stalls remain for long-lived streams.
raj (network): DNS SERVFAILs persist for ~7% of queries still. Investigating upstream resolver health and local DNS cache eviction patterns. Rolling restart of local dnsmasq on edge hosts to flush bad cached entries.
sam (eng-runtime): For the lingering stalls, we traced kv-cache eviction on some runtime shard when TLS handshake backlog spikes; increasing handshake worker threads helped. Deployed change to 10% of runtime hosts as canary.
laura (oncall): Customer impact assessment: a handful of streams experienced partial stalls resulting in retransmits and truncated final tokens. Estimated affected sessions ~0.4% of total during window (approx 3k sessions). No data loss; requests retried successfully in most cases.
emily (support): Logged details for the customer who reported case #C-4128 and offered workaround (retry or use non-streaming endpoint for critical batches).
mike (sre): Metrics now: p95=160ms, p99=220ms, tail-stalls count down 85% from peak. Streaming success rate back to 99.6%.
raj (network): Root cause hypothesis: simultaneous NAT ephemeral pressure + transient DNS resolver instability caused handshake amplification and packet retransmits on cross-AZ egress paths. Contributing factor: recent BGP path preference change in az-b that increased inter-zone hairpinning.
laura (oncall): Next actions: 1) keep nat-2 weighted 30% for 2h 2) rollout conntrack permanent config and monitor 3) open follow-up ticket with network team to revert BGP tweak and harden resolver config 4) run customer impact postmortem.
mike (sre): I'll create a postmortem draft and include timeline, root cause, mitigations, and KPIs. Also add a task to add automated ephemeral port alerting.
emily (support): I'll follow up with the impacted customers and confirm resolution.
incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED -> degraded for now; auto-close will not happen until laura confirms.
laura (oncall): Closing the page for now — system stable and p99 within SLO. Keep monitoring and move to P1->P2 follow-up. Thanks team :thumbsup:
